solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Show off magnificent bear

parts.note: grand means splendid or magnificent
to stand something is to bear or tolerate it

explanation.surface: A splendid bear is put on display, as at a zoo or a circus.
explanation.definitionFit: To grandstand is to behave ostentatiously to impress onlookers, the same verb sense as showing off.

clue.text: Fair girl at first sang all day — every second

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word girl is used
the second letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: At a fair, a girl first sang all day long, every second of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gala is a festive fair or celebration, such as a fete or carnival.

clue.text: One making a trunk call has no such complaint

definitions.text: One making a trunk call has no such complaint

parts.words: One making a trunk call has no such complaint
parts.note: a trunk call is an old British term for a long-distance phone call, but here it is an elephant trumpeting, and elephants never forget

explanation.surface: Someone placing a long-distance phone call is free of some ailment.
explanation.walkthrough: A trunk call is an old British phrase for a long-distance phone call; here the trunk is an elephant's, and the proverb says an elephant never forgets.
explanation.definitionFit: Loss of memory is the complaint an elephant proverbially never suffers.

clue.text: Exotic land set to encourage operator on bridge?

indicators.note: exotic means strange or foreign, so the letters are put into a strange order

parts.note: to urge on is to encourage

explanation.surface: A foreign country is set to cheer on a card player at the bridge table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'operator on bridge' suggests a card player or ship's officer; the bridge is dental work.
explanation.definitionFit: A dentist who operates fits dental bridges, so a bridge is something this specialist works on.

clue.text: Collapse following race, a sign of distress?

indicators.note: the word for collapse comes after the word for race

parts.note: to tear is to race or rush along
to drop is to collapse

explanation.surface: A runner collapses after a race, clearly in distress.
explanation.definitionFit: A single tear falling from the eye is a visible signal of sadness.

clue.text: Former African place of birth

definitions.meaning: a former province of South Africa
relating to the time or place of being born

explanation.definitionFit: This was a province of South Africa until 1994, and as an adjective the word means relating to being born.

clue.text: Cockpit in good condition

definitions.meaning: on a yacht the cockpit is the sunken area of deck where the helmsman sits, also called by this nautical name

explanation.definitionFit: A boat's sunken steering area has this nautical name, and the same word is an adjective for being healthy.

clue.text: Bucolic European block primarily upset by English

parts.note: to clog is to block

indicators.note: primarily takes only the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A rustic European bloc is upset, primarily by the English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bucolic' is here a noun, a pastoral poem, not the adjective it looks like.
explanation.definitionFit: A bucolic, used as a noun, is a pastoral poem, and this short pastoral poem is one, like Virgil's.

clue.text: Works in university, making contribution to reprint of rare title

indicators.note: a reprint sets the letters in type again, here in a new order

explanation.surface: A university contributes to the reprinting of a rare book title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in university, making contribution to' means U is added to the letters of RARE TITLE before 'reprint of' rearranges them all.
explanation.definitionFit: Written works, collectively, such as novels, plays and poems, form a body of writing.

clue.text: Online news partly fabricated? This is

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sceptic wonders whether internet stories are made up, and answers that they are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fabricated' is the surface's sense of made up, but read as a pun it means made into fabric: this cloth is a fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Flax cloth is a woven fabric, so it is something literally fabricated, with a pun on invented.

clue.text: George I put on gold crown, meeting destiny

indicators.note: I is placed on, that is after, the gold and the crown

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
the crown of something is its top
your lot is your fate or destiny

explanation.surface: A King George puts on a golden crown and meets his fate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'George' looks like one of the English kings named in the surface; it is the old jocular name pilots give the automatic flying system.
explanation.definitionFit: George is airmen's slang for the automatic pilot that flies a plane unattended.

clue.text: Talk about actors in cast getting put off

indicators.note: about says the word for talk goes around the other letters

parts.note: to prate is to talk at length foolishly

indicators.note: cast in the sense of thrown about, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Chatter about actors in a cast who are being postponed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like the actors' company but rearranges ACTORS IN, and 'about' puts PRATE round them.
explanation.definitionFit: To delay or postpone doing something, out of habit, is a synonym for putting it off.

clue.text: Muck-raker to run down mother entwined with one having desire?

parts.note: to scan a list is to run your eye down it

indicators.note: the two words are twisted together where they meet, so their touching letters cross over

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal
a longer is someone who longs for something

explanation.surface: A sleazy journalist disparages a mother who is tangled up with a lustful lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entwined with' means the two words interlock where they meet: the last letter of the first and the first letter of the second cross over, rather than simply sitting side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A muck-raker digs up dirt on people, which is what a spreader of gossip and scandal does.

clue.text: Face panic in hospital department that's besieged in the afternoon

indicators.note: the combination besieges, or surrounds, the afternoon abbreviation
the word for panic goes in the department

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital
a scare is a sudden panic
p.m. means in the afternoon

explanation.surface: Someone faces panic in a hospital department that is besieged in the afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's besieged' is loose grammar: the panic-in-department combination does the besieging, surrounding the afternoon abbreviation rather than sitting inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A steep slope or cliff edge is a rock face.

clue.text: Food's sizzling, still

parts.note: snap is a northern English word for a packed lunch, plus the 's
sizzling means very hot

explanation.surface: Someone announces that the food is sizzling in the pan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' reads as an adverb in the surface but is a noun: a still photograph. SNAP is northern English dialect for food taken to work.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick informal photograph is a still picture, as opposed to film.

clue.text: About to cut one half of starched tight collar

indicators.note: the short word cuts into the scrambled letters
tight in the sense of drunk, so those letters are in a mess
only the first of the two halves of the word starched is used

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone describes a stiff, tightly starched shirt collar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' is the anagram signal in its slang sense of drunk; 'collar' is police slang, not the shirt part the surface paints. The jumbled half reads ARST.
explanation.definitionFit: Police slang to collar someone is to seize and detain a suspect.

clue.text: Three-man government wanting judge to restrain current chief

indicators.note: the word for judge holds the others in, as a restraint

parts.note: to try a case is to judge it
i is the symbol for electric current
arch means chief or principal, as in arch-rival

explanation.surface: A triumvirate wants a judge to rein in the current chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Rule by three people jointly, like a triumvirate, is a form of government.

clue.text: Imbibe six-pack brother rejected

parts.note: a six-pack is a set of well-defined abdominal muscles, or abs

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the word is written backwards

explanation.surface: A brother turns down an offer of a six-pack of beer to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six-pack' suggests beer cans to go with 'Imbibe', but it is the muscles.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbibe is to take in or soak up, like a sponge does.

clue.text: Wacky single short guy, not one to get close

indicators.note: wacky means crazy, so the letters are jumbled
not means the letter for one is left out
short loses its last letter

parts.note: i is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A crazy single fellow, short of stature, is not someone to get close to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts guy to GU; 'not one' drops I from SINGLEGU, and 'Wacky' shuffles what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: To snuggle is to nestle or cuddle up close to someone.

clue.text: It may support rider put out by legal profession

parts.note: put out means annoyed or angry
the Bar is the profession of barristers

explanation.surface: A rider on horseback is displaced by lawyers.
explanation.definitionFit: On a man's bicycle the horizontal top tube between saddle and handlebars bears the cyclist, so it supports a rider.

clue.text: Laurel and Hardy on vacation, boarding British plane?

indicators.note: the letters go aboard, inside, the other pieces

parts.note: a plane is an example of a tree, hence the question mark

indicators.note: vacated, or emptied, leaves only the outer letters of the phrase

explanation.surface: The comedy duo Laurel and Hardy take a holiday, boarding a British aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laurel' looks like Stan Laurel of the duo but is the plant. 'on vacation' empties AND HARDY to AY, which 'boarding' puts into B + TREE.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet bay, whose leaves flavour cooking, is the laurel of classical wreaths.

clue.text: Caution Mrs Grundy — time to stop mixing in Italy

parts.note: Mrs Grundy, from an 18th-century play, is the type of the narrow-minded prig

indicators.note: the single letter stops up, or plugs, the jumbled letters
mixing says the letters of in Italy are stirred together

explanation.surface: A warning to a prim lady: it is time to stop mingling with people in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixing' rearranges IN ITALY and 'to stop' plugs T into the result.
explanation.definitionFit: This rare abstract noun means prudence, the quality of being careful, so it is a synonym of caution.

clue.text: Section of dramatically rising river

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means the letters read upwards, backwards
a section is a piece cut from the word that follows

explanation.surface: A section of river is dramatically rising in a flood.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tamar is the river dividing Devon and Cornwall in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: This river forms most of the border between Devon and Cornwall in south-west England.

clue.text: Comparatively small book anybody perused on a regular basis

indicators.note: reading the word at regular intervals picks every third letter of it

explanation.surface: A smaller book that anybody would read regularly.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, as in baby carrots, it describes a smaller-than-usual version of something.

clue.text: Maximising efficiency of new income for harnessing source of renewable energy

indicators.note: the jumbled letters harness, or hold within them, the other pieces
new says the letters of income are made over in a new order
the source of a word is its first letter

parts.note: go means energy or vitality

explanation.surface: A new source of income comes from tapping renewable energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges INCOME, which then holds R (from 'source of renewable') and GO.
explanation.definitionFit: Design that fits work to people to make it as efficient and comfortable as possible is described by this adjective.

clue.text: Abandon a missing black vessel

indicators.note: the letter for black is absent from the combined pieces

parts.note: to abort a plan is to abandon it
b is the abbreviation for black on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone is told to give up on a missing black item.
explanation.definitionFit: The main artery leading from the heart is a blood vessel.

clue.text: Quaint material left by duke

indicators.note: the duke has left, departing from the cloth's name

parts.note: tweed is a woollen cloth

explanation.surface: A duke's quaint old cloth has been abandoned.
explanation.definitionFit: Twee means affectedly dainty or quaint, a British informal adjective.

clue.text: Man perhaps mostly set on interrupting extremely ghastly old poem

indicators.note: the pieces break into the middle of the outer letters
extremely takes only the extreme, outer letters of the word

parts.note: Ray is an example of a man's name

indicators.note: the last letter of the word set is dropped

parts.note: on, or leg, is the leg side of a cricket field

explanation.surface: An ugly old poem is mostly about a man, perhaps one from the Isle of Man.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side is also called the leg side, so 'on' gives LEG. 'mostly' cuts set to SE, and 'extremely' takes GY from ghastly.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Gray's 1751 Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard is a famous eighteenth-century poem, known by this short title.
